page.text:
A *linear transformation* (or linear map) $T : V \to W$ between vector spaces
over the same field $F$ is a function that preserves vector addition and scalar
multiplication:
$$ T(u + v) = T(u) + T(v) \quad \text{and} \quad T(c \cdot v) = c \cdot T(v). $$
Equivalently, $T$ preserves all linear combinations: $T(\sum c_i v_i) = \sum c_i T(v_i)$.
Linear maps are the structure-preserving morphisms of linear algebra, forming
the vector space $\mathcal{L}(V, W) = \operatorname{Hom}_F(V, W)$ under pointwise
addition and scalar scaling.
